title: Chapter 100
content:
The moment the axe left his hand, Jakyeong snatched the sidearm from Director Kim’s waistband and pressed the muzzle straight against the man's temple.

Chairman Kang collapsed to the concrete floor with a heavy, sickening thud. Jakyeong glanced over his shoulder at Il-hyun.

"Sorry. Looks like you're an orphan now."

A flicker of raw, unadulterated ecstasy washed over Il-hyun’s face. Watching his biological father drop with an axe lodged deep in his skull didn't draw a single trace of grief or horror—only dark, intoxicating relief. On the floor, the old patriarch twitched in violent spasms, choking out wet, broken groans, while his stunned enforcers scrambled to raise their muzzles toward Jakyeong.

With guns drawn in a suffocating Mexican standoff, Director Kim shrieked at the top of his lungs:

"What are you standing around for?! The Chairman! Secure the Chairman, you useless bastards!"

Hired guns and private mercenaries made up the bulk of the detail, and panic fractured their ranks instantly. Jakyeong projected his voice over the chaos, cold and commanding:

"Think carefully. The man signing your checks is bleeding out on the floor. Turning this into a bloodbath is a suicide run with zero payout."

As if on cue, the violent twitching in Chairman Kang’s limbs slowed, fading into still silence. Several mercenaries traded uncertain glances, looking toward Director Kim. The director’s face was completely drained of color.

Keeping his weapon trained on the room, Jakyeong reached into Kim's inner jacket pocket, pulled out a tactical folding knife, and stepped behind Kang Il-hyun.

"CEO Kang right here will match your rate to the penny. Provided you lower those weapons."

Jakyeong sliced through the thick nylon cords, and Il-hyun pushed himself slowly to his feet. Director Kim turned stark white, frantically screaming at his men to hold their fire lest a stray round end his own life. Using Kim as a human shield, Jakyeong began stepping backward toward the corridor.

From the middle of the crowd, Takeya Jun drew his piece and pulled the trigger without a heartbeat's hesitation.

The gunshot cracked through the hollow concrete shell, the round grazing inches from Jakyeong’s cheek. Damn it.

Lowering his smoking barrel, Jun let out a hideous, blood-curdling sneer.

"Listen up, all of you! That's the bastard who took my eye! You think a dog like him leaves loose ends alive?"

Murmurs of unrest rippled through the mercenaries. As Jakyeong grimaced, Jun delivered the final blow:

"I'll foot the bill myself! Put both of those motherfuckers in the ground!"

Before Jakyeong could squeeze off a counter-shot, a second round tore straight through Director Kim’s skull. The man's head burst open, showering Jakyeong’s face and neck in hot, arterial spray.

Jakyeong fired back in rapid succession, using Kim’s limp corpse as a shield while dragging Il-hyun through the threshold and out into the stairwell.

Dumping the dead weight on the landing, they sprinted down the concrete steps. Heavy boots thundered from the lower floors—Chairman Kang’s perimeter guards, drawn by the gunfire, were already surging up the shaft. Trapped between two converging forces, the pair cut hard into a side corridor, searching for cover.

The footsteps closed in fast. Spotting an opening, Il-hyun grabbed Jakyeong’s arm and hauled him into an unfinished corner office. Concrete pillars stood exposed amidst scattered drywall sheets, scaffolding, and stacks of construction supplies, with the exterior glass wall completely missing to the open air.

Il-hyun threw the deadbolt and backed away from the entrance. Outside, furious shouts and slamming boots converged on the door.

Il-hyun ran a rapid sweep over Jakyeong. The white t-shirt he’d worn for their afternoon date was ruined, soaked in dark crimson, with fresh blood welling continuously from defensive cuts along both of his forearms.

"Are you alright?"

Jakyeong gave a curt nod. I should be asking you that. Kang Il-hyun’s condition was just as battered.

Il-hyun scanned the room. Heavy industrial tools, arc welders, and pressurized gas cylinders lay abandoned among the gravel and dust. He dragged Jakyeong toward the open drop-off at the edge of the floor, looked down, and gripped his shoulders tight.

Looking over the ledge, Jakyeong spotted a frayed green safety net stretched several stories below, with a mountain of construction sand beneath it. He immediately caught Il-hyun’s train of thought. But the net looked weathered and brittle—hardly built to withstand the combined impact of two grown men. And whether the sandbank below could cushion the fall was a sheer gamble.

Violent thuds battered the locked door.

"In here! Break it down!"

The steel panel shuddered on its hinges, followed by a burst of automatic fire punching ragged holes through the metal. As sparks and ricochets tore through the frame, Il-hyun seized Jakyeong’s jaw and pulled him into a rough, bruising kiss.

Blood—neither knew whose—mingled hot and metallic between their lips.

Breaking away, Jakyeong grabbed Il-hyun’s arm in immediate protest.

"Wait. Dropping together from this height is—"

Il-hyun cut him off with a faint, breathless smile.

"Go on ahead and wait for me."

Jakyeong’s eyes went wide. "What the hell does that—"

Before the question could finish, Il-hyun shoved him backward over the ledge. Jakyeong reached out in blind panic, but Il-hyun had already stepped back from the drop, leaving Jakyeong plummeting into open space.

Jakyeong slammed into the safety netting; the dry fibers tore on impact, dumping him onto the steep slope of the sandbank below.

The sheer concussive shock knocked the wind from his lungs, leaving him winded and dazed, though his bones seemed miraculously intact.

Upstairs, Il-hyun snatched a heavy gas-powered concrete saw from the floor, hauling the pull-cord with brutal force. On the third pull, the motor roared to life, the diamond-tipped blade spinning into a terrifying, high-velocity blur.

He marched straight toward the breached entrance.

The lock sheared off, the door burst inward, and Il-hyun swung the whirring blade into the charging vanguard with indiscriminate savagery. Agonized shrieks tore through the hall as flesh and bone were pulverized in a fountain of blood.

Gunfire erupted from the corridor. Il-hyun staggered back, a bullet tearing through his right flank.

Fuck. Cursing through his teeth, he wrenched an automatic rifle from a falling mercenary and dove behind a load-bearing pillar. A hail of lead chewed into the concrete, raining pulverized dust and sharp aggregate across his back.

Leaning around the corner, Il-hyun returned fire in crisp, controlled bursts. Skulls shattered; bodies dropped into the gore. By the headcount, the bulk of the assault team was packed into the corridor.

Il-hyun shifted his sights toward the pressurized welding gas tanks staged behind the enemy line.

A stray round grazed his shoulder, throwing his aim off. The bullet sparked harmlessly against the concrete, and the moment he pulled back into cover, Takeya Jun’s mocking voice echoed over the gunfire:

"Look at the arrogant young master, cornered like a trapped rat! Tell me... where did Lee Ja-kyeong scurry off to, huh?"

Il-hyun drew ragged, shuddering breaths. Looking down, dark blood was pumping heavily from his side. A detachment of gunmen moved toward the stairwell under Jun’s orders, clearly heading down to hunt Jakyeong.

Il-hyun leaned out, drilling clean rounds through their heads before they reached the landing. The instant they collapsed, a storm of lead hammered his concrete pillar, chipping away the cover until the rebar frame stood bare.

Panting heavily, Il-hyun’s mouth curved into a terrifying, blood-soaked grin.

"None of you are leaving this floor alive!"

He unleashed a relentless barrage toward the entrance, forcing the mercenaries to scramble behind opposing pillars. Buy time. Give Ja-kyeong every second he needs to clear the perimeter.

Dropping the empty magazine, Il-hyun checked his remaining rounds. He was running on fumes. The pressurized tanks behind Jun were obscured from this angle; hitting the valves required stepping entirely outside the pillar's shadow.

Stepping out meant drawing lethal crossfire. But hesitating meant Jun’s men would flank the floor, hunt down Jakyeong, and slaughter him in the dirt.

That is never going to happen. You're walking out of here alive, no matter what it takes.

A bitter, self-deprecating chuckle slipped past his bloody lips.

Fuck... if I knew I was checking out this early, I would've rewritten the damn will. That idiot lawyer better not take the 'buried together' clause literally.

He made his choice.

Air felt impossible to drag into his lungs, cold sweat plastering his hair to his forehead. Between the blood loss and the exhaustion, his vision was tunneling to black. Drawing one final, steady breath, he stepped out from behind the pillar into the open line of fire.

He fired two rapid shots to suppress the front rank, then aligned his iron sights onto the cluster of gas tanks.

Crack!

The round found its mark, but an incoming slug slammed hard into his right abdomen at the exact same instant. Il-hyun gasped, his knees buckling under the impact.

A high-pitched hiss of escaping gas filled the room. Takeya Jun’s lone eye met Il-hyun’s in pure, paralyzed horror.

Il-hyun squeezed the trigger a second time and threw his weight backward into cover.

A deafening, earth-shattering explosion ripped through the upper floor. The ceiling buckled, and slabs of flaming concrete rained down in a suffocating wall of fire.

Down on the sand pile, Jakyeong scrambled to his feet, snapping his head toward the upper level.

"Kang Il-hyun, you crazy bastard... You fucking psychotic piece of shit!"

He tried to spring to his feet, but his left leg gave out with a sharp, sickening spike of pain. It wasn't clean through, but the bone was deeply fractured. Gritting his teeth, he dragged himself up and limped frantically toward the building entrance.

Across the open lot, a convoy of black sedans roared through the perimeter gates, accompanied by several high-speed ambulances kicking up dust. Whether they were reinforcements or hostiles was a detail he didn't have time to verify.

Jakyeong dragged his fractured leg across the concrete threshold. He reached for the stairwell railing, hauling himself upward step by grueling step—just as a thunderous blast tore through the upper levels above him.

The structure shuddered violently. Concrete dust and structural debris cascaded down the stairwell like hail.

A cold, suffocating terror clamped around Jakyeong’s chest. No... Don't you dare.

Forgetting the agony in his leg entirely, he charged up the concrete flight like a madman.

From the ground floor below, an urgent voice bellowed up the shaft:

"Wei!"

Jakyeong froze mid-stride, glancing down.

Park Tae-soo, Wang Han, and Wang Ryun had breached the building, flanked by a squad of heavily armed operators. Even Tae-soo’s usually impenetrable mask was cracked with frantic tension.

Seeing Jakyeong caked in blood, Han shouted in alarm, but Jakyeong ignored them, staring up at the stairwell.

Emerging from the gloom, dragging his shattered body across the concrete, was Kang Il-hyun.

His clothes were shredded, his frame perforated with multiple gunshot wounds, leaving a dark, continuous trail of crimson in his wake with every agonizing step.

Catching sight of Jakyeong waiting below, a faint, exhausted smile touched the CEO's lips.

"Good... You're safe, my love..."

The words broke off as a thick gout of dark blood surged from his mouth.

Jakyeong felt his heart literally stop beating.

"You're... you're intact... My darling..."

With that final, whispered confession, Il-hyun’s eyes rolled back, and his towering frame collapsed forward, tumbling down the concrete steps toward Jakyeong.

"President Kang!"

Park Tae-soo sprinted forward, but Jakyeong was already there—dropping to his knees, catching the heavy, cooling body in his arms.

The air reeked of copper and ash. Il-hyun’s skin felt terrifyingly cold—the sickening texture of holding a corpse.

The world around them dissolved into white noise.

Clasping the ruined frame against his chest, Jakyeong’s voice fractured into a broken, breathless sob:

"Hey... Kang Il-hyun..."

No reply.

Even the shallow, ragged wheeze he had clung to a second ago had vanished into the silence.
